rau-mam-da-sa-pa-luoc-xi-dau.name: Sa Pa Stone Mustard Greens with Soy Dip
aliases: Boiled Sa Pa stone mustard greens with soy sauce
Stone mustard greens with garlic soy dip
rau-mam-da-sa-pa-luoc-xi-dau.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person family meal.
rau-mam-da-sa-pa-luoc-xi-dau.description: Sa Pa stone mustard greens have crisp stems and a mild sweetness. A quick boil and garlic-chili soy dip make a simple side for a home meal.
rau-mam-da-sa-pa-luoc-xi-dau.finished_dish: The stems are tender yet crisp and bright green; the soy dip is gently savory with fragrant garlic.
rau-mam-da-sa-pa-luoc-xi-dau.serving: Drain the greens and serve with the soy dip alongside rice and a braised or pan-fried dish.
tips: Choose fresh firm shoots without bruising.
Avoid overboiling so the greens stay crisp.
Add soy sauce gradually because saltiness varies by brand.

rau-mam-da-sa-pa-luoc-xi-dau.time_note: About 16 minutes; boiling time varies with the size and tenderness of the shoots.

ingredients.name: Stone mustard greens
ingredients.notes: Trim tough parts and keep tender stems and leaves.

preparation_steps: Remove bruised leaves and tough stems. Rinse gently several times and drain; separate oversized buds for even cooking.
Mince the garlic and chili. Stir soy sauce with sugar and a spoonful of warm water, then add the aromatics.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the greens and boil for about 3–5 minutes; check the stems and remove when just tender.
Drain the greens, arrange on a plate, and serve with the garlic-chili soy dip.

rau-sam-luoc-cham-nuoc-mam-toi-hue.name: Hue Boiled Purslane with Garlic Fish Sauce
aliases: Hue rau sam with garlic fish sauce
Boiled purslane with garlic fish sauce
rau-sam-luoc-cham-nuoc-mam-toi-hue.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person family meal.
rau-sam-luoc-cham-nuoc-mam-toi-hue.description: Boiled purslane is a rustic vegetable dish noted in Hue food culture. Tender greens retain a fresh flavor and pair with fragrant garlic fish sauce.
rau-sam-luoc-cham-nuoc-mam-toi-hue.finished_dish: The stems are tender-crisp and the leaves remain intact; the dip is savory, garlicky and lightly tart.
rau-sam-luoc-cham-nuoc-mam-toi-hue.serving: Drain the greens and serve with garlic fish sauce as a vegetable side with steamed rice.
tips: Choose young, firm stems without yellowing.
Rinse gently to avoid bruising the leaves.
Season the fish sauce first, then add lime and sugar gradually.

rau-sam-luoc-cham-nuoc-mam-toi-hue.time_note: About 15 minutes; boiling time varies with the tenderness of the greens.

ingredients.name: Purslane
ingredients.notes: Trim old roots and damaged stems.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the sour and salty flavors.

preparation_steps: Trim roots and old stems. Rinse the greens several times in clean water and drain.
Mince the garlic and chili. Stir fish sauce with sugar and lime juice, add the aromatics, and taste.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the purslane and boil for about 2–3 minutes, until the stems are just tender; drain.
Arrange the greens on a plate and serve with garlic fish sauce. For a fully plant-based version, replace fish sauce with soy sauce.

ngon-su-su-luoc-cham-mam-toi-ot-tam-dao.name: Tam Đảo Chayote Shoots with Garlic-Chili Fish Sauce
aliases: Boiled chayote shoots with garlic chili fish sauce
ngon-su-su-luoc-cham-mam-toi-ot-tam-dao.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person family meal.
ngon-su-su-luoc-cham-mam-toi-ot-tam-dao.description: Young Tam Đảo chayote shoots are quickly boiled to keep their green color and crisp sweetness. A garlic-chili fish sauce dip gives this familiar mountain vegetable a savory finish.
ngon-su-su-luoc-cham-mam-toi-ot-tam-dao.finished_dish: The leaves are tender and the stems remain crisp; the dip has fragrant garlic, chili and a light sweet-sour balance.
ngon-su-su-luoc-cham-mam-toi-ot-tam-dao.serving: Drain the greens, arrange on a plate and serve warm with the garlic-chili dip alongside rice and a savory dish.
tips: Choose young shoots with green leaves and non-fibrous stems.
Peel fibers from older stems and snap into serving lengths.
Boil in rapidly simmering water and avoid overcooking.

ingredients.name: Young chayote shoots
ingredients.notes: Peel fibers from older stems and snap into serving lengths.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the sour and salty flavors.

preparation_steps: Snap the shoots into serving lengths, remove yellow leaves and fibrous stems, rinse and drain.
Mince the garlic and chili. Stir fish sauce with sugar, lime juice and a spoonful of warm water, then add the aromatics.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the shoots and boil for about 4–6 minutes; check the stems for tenderness.
Drain the shoots, arrange on a plate and serve with the garlic-chili fish sauce.

rau-bo-khai-luoc-ba-be.name: Ba Bể Boiled Bò Khai Wild Greens
aliases: Boiled bò khai greens from Ba Bể
Bắc Kạn bò khai greens with garlic fish sauce
rau-bo-khai-luoc-ba-be.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side for a four-person family meal.
rau-bo-khai-luoc-ba-be.description: Bò khai is a wild green associated with Ba Bể, Bắc Kạn. A brief boil keeps the shoots green and crisp; Bếp Việt pairs them with a garlic-chili dip for a home meal.
rau-bo-khai-luoc-ba-be.finished_dish: The deep-green shoots are tender yet crisp with their characteristic wild-green aroma; the dip is savory and fragrant.
rau-bo-khai-luoc-ba-be.serving: Drain the greens and serve with garlic-chili fish sauce and steamed rice.
tips: Rinse and gently rub the greens as described in the source to reduce their distinctive aroma.
Serve soon after boiling rather than leaving the greens in hot water.

rau-bo-khai-luoc-ba-be.time_note: About 22 minutes; boiling time varies with the stems.

ingredients.name: Bò khai greens
ingredients.notes: Trim fibrous stems, rinse and gently rub.

preparation_steps: Remove fibrous stems and damaged leaves. Rinse well, gently rub along the stems as described by the source, rinse again and drain.
Mince the garlic and chili. Mix fish sauce with lime juice and a spoonful of warm water.
cooking_steps: Bring salted water to a boil. Add the greens and boil for about 3–5 minutes, until the stems are just tender; remove promptly.
Drain the greens, arrange on a plate and serve with the garlic-chili fish sauce.

bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.name: Southern Vietnamese Pumpkin Blossoms with Kho Quẹt
aliases: Boiled pumpkin blossoms with kho quẹt
Bông bí luộc ăn cùng kho quẹt miền Tây
bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.serving_basis: A shared vegetable side with dipping sauce for a four-person family meal.
bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.description: Tender-crisp pumpkin blossoms served with thick, savory-sweet kho quẹt are a rustic pairing in Southern Vietnamese home cooking. Bếp Việt standardizes the vegetable and dip portions for four.
bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.finished_dish: The petals are tender and the stems lightly crisp; kho quẹt is thick, savory-sweet, fragrant with pepper and dried shrimp.
bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.serving: Arrange the blossoms on a platter and serve the kho quẹt in a bowl for dipping. Eat warm with steamed rice.
tips: Choose fresh flowers with firm stems and no bruised petals.
Rinse gently so the petals do not tear; remove the stamens if the flowers are large.
Simmer the kho quẹt over low heat until glossy, then adjust the seasoning.

bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.image_alt: A platter of golden pumpkin blossoms beside a bowl of glossy kho quẹt with pork and dried shrimp.
bong-bi-luoc-cham-kho-quet.time_note: About 33 minutes; boiling time varies with blossom size.

ingredients.name: Young pumpkin blossoms
ingredients.notes: Remove tough stem ends and stamens if needed.

preparation_steps: Trim the blossoms, remove fibrous stem ends and discard damaged petals. Rinse quickly and drain.
Soak the dried shrimp until soft and rinse again. Dice the pork belly, mince the shallot and crush the pepper.
cooking_steps: Render the pork belly in a pan over medium heat until lightly golden. Add shallot and dried shrimp and stir until fragrant.
Add fish sauce, sugar and 100 ml water. Simmer over low heat until glossy and thick; season with pepper and chili.
Bring the remaining water to a boil. Add pumpkin blossoms and boil for about 2–3 minutes until the stems are just tender. Drain and serve with kho quẹt.
